root_idea.summary: The root centers on removal, driving away, and forcing something to withdraw.
root_idea.development: The core sense of expelling develops into withdrawal at a distance, a resulting state of humiliation or contempt, and the recoiling or dimming of sight. Related derived usages include mutual stone-throwing and gambling.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form rather than the Quranic imperative.
Displayed under the normalized active-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To drive away, repel, or chide away; in the imperative, to order someone to go away or be gone.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic imperative expresses removal to a distance with anger. The same lexical branch also has an intransitive use meaning to go away after being driven away or chidden.

senses.definition: Repelled, driven away, or made to withdraw.
senses.usage_conditions: An active-participial or adjectival description of one forced away or kept at a distance; in the Quranic plural expression, it describes a repelled state.
An adjectival description of a humiliated or disgraced state, including the Quranic plural description of the transformed people.

senses.definition: Of the sight: recoiling or withdrawing in humiliation; dazzled, confused, or dim.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic expression describing the returning gaze. The lexical evidence reports recoiling, withdrawal, contemptibility, and impaired sight as interpretive alternatives of this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vile, despised, hated, or abject.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or secondary verbal extension from being driven away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sight, to become dazzled, confused, or dim.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of the verb to visual perception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw stones at one another or engage in mutual stone-throwing.
To contend in a game of hazard; to gamble.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to wool of poor quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Driven away, repelled, and not suffered to approach people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific conventional application to a dog, swine, or devil.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Driving away and chiding are covered by the Quranic verb sense.
The intransitive withdrawal use is covered by the broader verb sense.
The Quranic imperative of angry removal is directly represented.
The figurative verbal meaning of becoming vile or despised is separately retained.
The verbal application to dazzled or dim sight is retained.
Mutual stone-throwing is retained as a derived classical usage.
The gambling usage is separately retained.
Pointer-only reference to the Form III entry.
Pointer-only reference to the Form I entry.
The independent lexical item for bad wool is retained.
The specific animal and devil application is retained separately from Quranic adjectival senses.
The contemptible or abject adjectival branch is represented.
All reported Quranic interpretations of the returning sight are covered.

cautions: The expression in 67:4 has several explicitly reported interpretations: a recoiling or withdrawing gaze, a contemptible or repelled gaze, and dazzled, confused, or dim sight.
